answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified stake rather than the number of agent accounts. For example, an agent must lock a deposit to submit a forecast, and earns reputation only when its forecast is later checked against an external outcome; copied identities cannot multiply that stake or the evidence. An attacker can still create a comet, sparrow, or spiral of fake agents, but must tie up real capital per claim and risks losing it when claims fail.
